children.summary: This page is the beginning of the corrected transcript for NVIDIA Corp.'s Q4 2026 Earnings Call, dated February 25, 2026. It features the opening remarks by Operator Sarah and Toshiya Hari (VP of Investor Relations), who introduce the speakers Jensen Huang and Colette Kress. The text includes standard legal disclaimers regarding forward-looking statements and non-GAAP financial measures before handing over to CFO Colette M. Kress. Kress begins her section by reporting record revenue of $68 billion for the quarter, a 73% year-over-year increase, driven largely by data center growth. This page is a transcript from NVIDIA Corp.'s Q4 2026 Earnings Call, discussing the company's financial performance and technological advancements. It highlights strong data center revenue growth driven by Blackwell and Hopper products, significant R&D investment, and the success of networking solutions like NVLink and Spectrum-X Ethernet. The text also details customer adoption of AI infrastructure, specifically mentioning Meta's use of NVIDIA technology for their GEM model. This page is a segment of the corrected transcript for NVIDIA Corp.'s Q4 2026 Earnings Call. It details financial performance and strategic updates, including sovereign AI growth driven by customers in Canada, France, and the UK; the unveiling of the new Rubin platform at CES; and strong gaming revenue of $3.7 billion. The text also covers advancements in Professional Visualization, noting a record $1.3 billion in revenue. This page is a segment of the NVIDIA Corp. Q4 2026 Earnings Call transcript, focusing on financial performance and strategic outlook. It details automotive revenue growth driven by self-driving solutions and the introduction of the 'Alpamayo' AI portfolio. The text highlights significant contributions from Physical AI, listing key commercial partners like Waymo and Tesla, as well as industrial robotics collaborations with companies such as Boston Dynamics and Siemens. Financial metrics provided include GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins, operating expenses, free cash flow generation, and shareholder returns. The document concludes with the first-quarter outlook, projecting total revenue of $78 billion and noting that Data Center compute revenue from China is excluded from these forecasts.

children.title: Harlan Sur
children.path: NVDA Q4 FY26 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Harlan Sur
children.summary: Harlan Sur, an analyst from JPMorgan Securities LLC, asks about the growth of networking revenues in NVIDIA's data center profile. He references a 3.6x year-over-year growth rate and discusses the annualized run rate of the Spectrum-X Ethernet Switching platform, noting it may have increased from $10 billion to around $11-12 billion in the second half of the previous year. He also inquires about the future trend of the Spectrum run rate given upcoming launches like the 102T Spectrum-6 Switching platforms.

children.title: C.J. Muse
children.path: NVDA Q4 FY26 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/C.J. Muse
children.summary: This page is a transcript from NVIDIA Corp.'s Q4 2026 Earnings Call, dated February 25, 2026. It features a discussion on the company's networking business growth driven by NVLink and Spectrum-X Ethernet, followed by a Q&A session. Analyst C.J. Muse asks about future roadmaps regarding customized silicon and dielet architecture. Jen Hsun Huang responds by explaining the latency benefits of avoiding dielets where possible, referencing the Grace Blackwell and Rubin architectures, and highlighting the efficiency of CUDA.

children.title: Stacy A. Rasgon
children.path: NVDA Q4 FY26 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Stacy A. Rasgon
children.summary: Stacy A. Rasgon, an analyst from Bernstein Research, asks two questions regarding NVIDIA's financial outlook. First, he inquires about the sequential growth trajectory for the year, specifically questioning if the massive acceleration seen with Blackwell will continue as Rubin ramps up in the back half of the year. Second, he asks for expectations regarding gaming revenue growth in fiscal 2027, noting potential pressure due to memory constraints.

children.title: Colette M. Kress
children.path: NVDA Q4 FY26 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Colette M. Kress
children.summary: Colette M. Kress responds to Stacy Rasgon's questions regarding NVIDIA's revenue outlook and product roadmap. She discusses the simultaneous sales of Blackwell architecture and the upcoming market entry of Vera Rubin, noting strong customer demand but uncertainty on the exact ramp timing in the second half of the year. Additionally, she addresses gaming sector expectations, stating that supply will remain tight for a few quarters, making year-over-year growth projections too early to determine at this time.

children.title: Mark Lipacis
children.path: NVDA Q4 FY26 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Mark Lipacis
children.summary: The section titled 'Mark Lipacis' features a question from Mark Lipacis, an analyst at Evercore Group LLC, directed at NVIDIA executives. He asks for clarification on revenue diversification, specifically regarding the growth of non-hyperscale customers compared to hyperscalers and whether this trend is expected to continue. The section includes responses from Colette M. Kress (CFO) confirming that while hyperscalers make up about 50% of revenue, there is significant diversity in other customer types like AI model makers and enterprises. Jen Hsun Huang (CEO) adds that NVIDIA's ecosystem advantage lies in its CUDA platform's availability across various sectors including cloud, edge, telecommunications, robotics, and self-driving cars.

children.title: Aaron Rakers
children.path: NVDA Q4 FY26 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Aaron Rakers
children.summary: In this section, analyst Aaron Rakers of Wells Fargo asks about the strategic importance of NVIDIA's Vera CPUs in the company's architecture evolution, specifically regarding their role as a standalone solution for inference workloads. Jen Hsun Huang responds by explaining that Vera is designed with unique architectural decisions to support LPDDR5 and deliver exceptional single-threaded performance and bandwidth. He emphasizes that these features are critical for data-driven AI tasks, particularly for post-training phases where CPU-only environments are often used.
